title: Direct assessment of liver glycogen storage by 13C nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy and regulation of glucose homeostasis after a mixed meal in normal subjects
authors: Taylor R, Magnusson I, Rothman DL, Cline GW, Caumo A, Cobelli C, et al.
population: Healthy adults aged 18 to 40 years: 8 in the liver glycogen study, 6 in the hepatic glucose output study and 6 in the glycogen pathway study; two subjects took part in two studies
funder: The work was funded by the Public Health Service (DK49230, DK45735, RR-03475, RR-00125), a grant from the American Diabetes Association (G. I. Shulman), and a grant from the Juvenile Diabetes Foundation (I. Magnusson). It was also partially supported by a grant from the Italian Ministero della Universita e della Ricerca Scientifica e Tecnologica and by grant 9300457PF40 from the Italian National Research Council. Roy Taylor was supported by Medical Research Council Grant G9012977SB.
inKindSupport: Purified acetaminophen glucuronide used as a standard was the gift of McNeil Pharmaceuticals.
result: Liver glycogen fell overnight from 350 ± 18 mmol/L 4 h after the evening meal to 207 ± 22 mmol/L in the fasting state. After an 824-kcal liquid meal with 67.3% of energy as glucose, it peaked at 316 ± 19 mmol/L at 318 ± 31 min; net hepatic glycogen synthesis was 28.3 ± 3.7 g, about 19% of the meal carbohydrate. Plasma insulin rose from 4.1 to 73 mU/L at 30 min. Hepatic glucose output, 1.90 ± 0.04 mg/kg per min fasting, was completely suppressed within 30 min and regained the fasting rate between 300 and 460 min after the meal (mean 380 ± 28 min). Mean liver volume 1.44 L.
